cases.note: TryParse, Dictionary.TryGetValue and ref on simple locals convert natively to existing `§A{out}`/`§A{ref}` and mutate caller storage on all four surfaces.
`out _` converts natively; `out var n` inside a conditional is kept as an inline `§CS{}` C# expression (counted as interop, effects assumed: Calor0419). #1427 decides native versus explicit refusal.
ref to an array element, a static field, and the same local twice (aliasing) convert natively and match. #1427 still owns the writable-lvalue and aliasing matrix.

Named/reordered `out`, `in`, and out-before-exception emit native modifiers, but the member fails on an unrelated empty-catch defect (X-TRYCATCH-01). Rescue paths (CLI, MCP passthroughOnError) preserve it as interop; MCP default returns isError (Calor1002, CS0161).
A by-reference call whose mutation is read later in the same expression keeps C# evaluation order.
Dictionary.TryGetValue with an int payload (a miss resets 99 to 0, so a copy would be visible) and a List<string> payload (a miss leaves null) converts natively and matches.

Generic `out T` and an `out` parameter with [NotNullWhen(true)]: the contract says these stay preserved or refused unless #1427 admits them. Rescue paths preserve `Probe`; MCP default converts natively and the compiler rejects `TryCast<str>(5, out s)` (Calor0208, isError). The attribute is carried as `[@NotNullWhen(true)]` with no flow meaning.

`Bump(ref pts[0].X)` on a struct array: the converter hoists `pts[0]` into a local copy and passes `ref _hoist001.X`. Reported native with no losses on all four surfaces; the default compile fails only on an unrelated Calor0410, and with --permissive-effects the result is 1 instead of 2. A copy masquerading as a by-reference argument.

Analysis row: by-reference mutation must invalidate pre-call nullability and contract facts and refuse or demote proofs. Not fixtured at R0; see 0.24 S1 `OBL-MUTATION-KILL` (PR #1480, undispositioned).
Analysis row: effect charging for mutation through `ref`/`out` and conservative handling of unresolved callees (#1427). Not fixtured at R0.
String targets: format specifier, alignment, escaped braces, null hole and hole evaluation order all match. Holes that contain calls compile as raw C# expressions with assumed effects (Calor0419).

FormattableString/IFormattable targets and a FormattableString-vs-object overload keep their C# target typing (the emitter re-emits `$"..."`). Default compile fails on an unrelated Calor0410 for `Kind(object)`; with --permissive-effects the behavior matches. FeatureSupport still says Full.

Custom interpolated-string handler: rescue paths preserve the handler type and `Probe`; MCP default converts the call natively, flattens the argument to STRING and fails (isError; Calor0208). Not silent, but not refused at conversion time.
Ordinary literals containing `${x}` and `{x}` stay literal (the converter escapes `\${x}`).

Native Calor: an undefined name inside `${...}` is now bound and reported (Calor0200), so the historical 'invisible to the binder' claim no longer holds; the diagnostic points at line 1, column 1, not the hole.

Native Calor: a call inside `${...}` in a function declared pure (`§E{}`) is a raw C# expression; the compiler accepts the declared effects as an assumption (Calor0419 warning) instead of checking them.

Culture: de-DE current culture through a string target and FormattableString.ToString(InvariantCulture) match. The default compile fails on an unrelated Calor0410 (the culture setter); the comparison uses --permissive-effects.
Competing overloads where target typing changes the selected method observably (string vs FormattableString vs IFormattable vs a handler), asserting the selected overload. Not fixtured at R0.
F-2 incomplete-binding counts over the corpus before and after the fix (#906 closure). Not measured at R0 (corpus not used).

String return target: `return $"...";` from a string-returning method, with format, alignment and culture, through original and generated execution. Not fixtured as a return at R0 (F2-INTERP-01 covers assignments).

The epic's `int Add(int x) => x + 1` row and a recursive local function: both members are preserved as `§CSHARP` (feature `method`), as #846 intended. Default compile then fails on Calor0410 in the caller; with --permissive-effects behavior matches. Native support is the 0.25 work.
C-1 shadowing shape: preserved as `§CSHARP`, no silent rebind (3|1002 matches). Still not native.

C-2 (shadows an inherited method), C-3 (shadows an overload), a forward call, and a delegate to a local function: all three members preserved as `§CSHARP`; behavior matches under --permissive-effects. Not native.
Outside the frozen slice: capturing, generic and iterator local functions stay preserved as `§CSHARP` on every surface; behavior matches under --permissive-effects. They must never count as native.
Analysis row: binding, effects and verification visit native local-function bodies and call edges, or refuse; no proof from omitted bodies (#847). Not fixtured at R0.
Async local functions (outside the frozen slice) stay preserved, never native. Not fixtured at R0.

Legal iterator property and indexer: the converter emits `§YIELD`/`§YBRK` in accessors; MCP default fails Calor0209 (isError). Rescue paths (CLI, MCP passthroughOnError) preserve both classes and match, including laziness.

Disposal and exceptions: an abandoned iterator property runs its finally; an iterator indexer throws on the second MoveNext. MCP default fails Calor0209; rescue paths preserve both, and behavior matches.
Native Calor with `§YIELD` in a property accessor (the MCP output of F4-ITER-01) keeps Calor0209.
The three historical FluentValidation modules (EmptyTester, NotEmptyTester, ITestValidationContinuation) through the pinned CLI with project references. Not re-run at R0.

Historical repro unchanged on the native path: `§ARR2D{arr2d004:arr2d005:Cell}` then `§R arr2d005` gives CS0201 and CS0103 `arr2d005` (plus CS1061 on `§IDX2D ... .V`). MCP default fails (isError); rescue paths preserve both classes. The epic's 'id/name repair already exists' does not hold for this shape.

Arrays as an argument and in conditional branches: the native output does not parse (Calor0106 unknown operator `?`), so even MCP default rescues `Probe` through the parse-failure path. Rescued output matches, including no evaluation of the unselected branch.
Statement-position 1-D and 2-D arrays bound to declared locals convert natively and match.

Name collision: in `Run` the converter hoists array elements into `_hoist000`, the name of a user local in the same scope; the native output is rejected (Calor0260, immutable binding rebound). Grid's parameters match the generated `§ARR2D` id and name. Exception order is observable only on rescue paths, where it matches.

Rank and initializer matrix in expression position (jagged, rank 3, sized with initializer, implicitly typed, array nested in an initializer): MCP default fails; rescue paths preserve `Probe` and match.
Declared supported/unsupported rank, initializer and element-type boundary (#1132 governing scope). F5-ARRAY-05 samples forms but does not define the boundary; the F5 PR must register it.
No-flag `calor convert` rescue is labeled '(2 via --passthrough fallback)' although no flag was passed.
No-flag and --passthrough runs produce the same JSON loss feature (`post-validation-fallback`) and the same text; no field records which trigger fired.

Default difference: CLI `calor convert` rescues by default (RescueUnusableMembers = true); MCP `calor_convert` with default arguments does not and returns isError; MCP with passthroughOnError rescues like the CLI. No output names the path that fired or the default that applied.
Project-level `calor migrate`: defaults, rescue/passthrough precedence, member/file/project aggregation, partial failure, exit code. Not exercised at R0.
MCP `calor_migrate` (MigrateTool sets PassthroughOnError = false): outcome, provenance and partial failure. Not exercised at R0.
MCP `calor_batch`: per-file and aggregate reporting, partial batch failure, protocol error behavior. Not exercised at R0.
Library and SDK wrappers (`ConversionOptions.RescueUnusableMembers` defaults to false): documented defaults and reported provenance. Not exercised at R0.
A fully native conversion reports no interop and prints no preservation attribution.
Converter-level interop without rescue (local functions, feature `method`) is reported without a rescue or passthrough attribution.
Exit status per documented mode, `--lossy`, and rejected outcomes across CLI and MCP. Not exercised at R0.

An unrelated option changes whether rescue fires: MCP `calor_convert` with passthroughOnError and a custom moduleName does not rescue F4-ITER-01 (isError), while the same call without moduleName does. The module name becomes the namespace identity that the rescue requires to match.
Both rescue and passthrough enabled versus rescue disabled, on every surface that exposes them; precedence when both fire. Not exercised beyond F6-REPORT-02/03.
Structured DTO and envelope schema: actual-trigger provenance field or a versioned compatible extension, and wire compatibility. Not exercised at R0.

#1428 shared control, F1 x F5. `Bump(ref pts[0].X)` passes a struct array element by reference. The converter hoists `pts[0]` into a local copy, passes `ref _hoist001.X`, and reports a native conversion with no losses on all four surfaces; with --permissive-effects the program returns 1 where C# returns 2. Expected: the element is passed by reference (result 2) on every surface, or the call is refused explicitly; never a silent copy. Owned by F1; re-run whenever F5 changes array-element hoisting.

#1428 shared control, F5 x F6. The F5-ARRAY-01 expression-position 2-D array: today the no-flag CLI rescues the member as `§CSHARP` and labels it '(2 via --passthrough fallback)', and MCP with default arguments fails (isError). Expected once both families land: native on all four surfaces, with no fallback loss feature and no rescue attribution; a shape F5 still refuses is reported with its actual trigger.

equals.firstError: '§YIELD' is illegal inside a property/indexer accessor.

cases.note: #1428 shared control, F4 x F6. The F4-ITER-01 iterator property and indexer: the native output carries `§YIELD` in an accessor and fails the compile with Calor0209; the CLI rescues it as a post-validation fallback, and MCP with default arguments returns isError. Expected: converter-level preservation on all four surfaces without rescue, reported by F6 as converter preservation, not as a post-validation fallback.

#1428 shared control, F2 x F6. The F2-INTERP-03 custom `[InterpolatedStringHandler]` call: the CLI rescues it as a post-validation fallback; MCP with default arguments returns isError. Expected: F2 refuses the handler at conversion time, so every surface preserves the member without rescue, and F6 reports that refusal as its trigger.

#1428 shared control, F1 x F3. A native local function with a `ref` or `out` parameter, called with `ref`/`out` arguments from its enclosing member, including one that assigns its `out` before throwing. Native output keeps by-reference identity and C# definite assignment, and analysis drops facts over the written argument (R-OBL, #1496); otherwise the enclosing member stays preserved. Not fixtured at 1.1.0.

#1428 shared control, F2 x F3. An interpolated string whose hole calls a native local function (`$"{Fmt(x)}"` with a local `string Fmt(int v)`). The hole binds to the local function, never to a same-named class member (F3-LOCAL-02), and its effects are charged to the enclosing member; a hole that cannot be bound keeps the member preserved. Not fixtured at 1.1.0.

#1428 shared control, F3 x F5. An expression-position array (a returned `new int[,] {{...}}` and an array argument) inside a native local function: the intersection of F3's native slice and F5's native array forms. Expected native: generated hoist and `§ARR2D` names do not collide with the local function's parameters or the enclosing member's locals, and element evaluation order matches C#. Whole-member preservation does not satisfy this row; a shape outside either family's native slice needs its own registered row. Not fixtured at 1.1.0.

#1428 shared control, F1 x F2. An `out var` declared inside an interpolation hole (`$"{(int.TryParse(s, out var n) ? n : -1)}"`). Inside the #1427 RO-DECL-1 bound the declaration lowers natively with C# scope and definite assignment; outside it the member stays preserved. Never inline `§CS{}` with assumed effects (the F1-REFOUT-02 shape). Not fixtured at 1.1.0.

#1429 row. The calls reference documents the ref/out/in call forms #1427 admits (`§A{out}`, `§A{ref}`, `§A{in}`, the `out _` discard, and the bounded `out var` lowering) with a complete program that compiles by default and whose generated C# keeps by-reference identity. The page has no such example at 1.1.0.

#1429 row. The string-operations reference documents interpolated strings: an undefined name in a hole is reported at the hole, and a converted C# interpolation keeps its target typing. Complete programs compile by default; a negative example is labeled as one.

#1429 row. The convert page says local functions no longer silently substitute a different construct. At the baseline F3-LOCAL-02 (a local `Add` shadowing a class method `Add`) is preserved as `§CSHARP` and returns the C# result, so the claim holds. It must keep holding when F3 converts local functions natively: native with the same result, or preserved; never rebound.

#1429 row. The structure-tags reference documents native local-function syntax with a complete program that compiles by default, including the shadowing rule (the local function wins over a same-named member).

#1429 row. The convert page documents that iterator properties and indexers are preserved at conversion time on every surface, with laziness, `finally` and exception timing kept, and that native `§YIELD` in an accessor stays Calor0209.

#1429 row. The convert page documents expression-position array conversion: supported ranks and initializers, the declared unsupported boundary (F5-ARRAY-06), and C# element evaluation order, with an example whose output compiles by default.

#1429 row. The convert page's Supported Constructs section says the command line preserves an unconvertible member as `§CSHARP` by default, without `--passthrough`. At the baseline the no-flag run does preserve F5-ARRAY-01's members, but labels them '(2 via --passthrough fallback)'. Expected: the page and the report name the same path.

#1429 row. The MCP page lists `calor_convert` without describing when it rescues a member. At the baseline MCP with default arguments rescues some members and not others: it rescues F5-ARRAY-02 (whose native output does not parse; `post-validation-fallback`), but returns isError on F4-ITER-01 (whose native output parses and the compiler rejects with Calor0209), which it rescues only with `passthroughOnError`. Expected: the page states the per-surface default for each trigger and the report names it.

discovered.note: Outside the six families. An empty catch clause followed by a statement: the converter emits an empty `§CA` clause and the compiler parses the next sibling statement into the catch body. Native, no losses, compiles, wrong result (1 instead of 2) on all four surfaces.

maintainerDecisions.decision: Accept the section 9 ceilings. Recorded by the merge of #1483 (16c1c5f8, 2026-10-04T00:05:35Z, merged by juanatjcx, the maintainer's authorized alternate login), which section 1 makes the acceptance, and written back by #1552. mappedBlockers.rule: A 0.24 S2 repair or demotion applies to a family when the family's native 0.25 work creates a construct the repair's change governs. Every repair in the S2 record has exactly one disposition here: applicable (with its PR, merge commit and regression witnesses) or not applicable (with a reason). Every applicable repair is merged on main; it blocks the family's READY until that record's blockersResolved entry cites the repair's merge commit and a retained witnessRun record under docs/plans/evidence/ showing its regression witnesses passed on the READY candidate (S007). A disposition is not a 0.25 repair, and 0.24 false proofs stay owned by 0.24.

applicable.reason: Entry facts are dropped when a body may write a name they read, including ref/out/in aliasing and element or field stores; raw C# makes a body opaque. F1 adds by-reference writes. F2, F3 and F5 replace raw C# that is opaque today (inline `§CS{}` interpolation holes with calls, preserved local functions, preserved array expressions) with native calls and element stores, so the fact-kill rule must cover them.

After a statement that may throw (calls, element reads, checked arithmetic) the obligation state is not exact. F1 adds calls that write `out` before throwing (F1-REFOUT-04); F2 lifts interpolation-hole calls into native calls; F3 adds native local-function calls; F5 adds native element initializers that may throw (F5-ARRAY-04).

String literals reach Z3 per UTF-16 code unit and null-tolerant string forms are refused when unsound. F2 changes what a string literal with `${...}` holes means (bound holes), so contract translation of interpolated strings must model the holes or refuse; it must not treat them as literal text.

notApplicable.reason: Literal cache keys. No family changes literal hashing; a node kind the hasher does not know is never cached (the SawUnhashedKind rule), so new F2-F5 expression forms cannot share a cache entry.

Interface/implementer implication prover. No family changes that channel. R-IMPL makes any string-, array- or user-type-sorted implication Assumed regardless of how the value was produced, so the 1.0.0 'uncertain' IMPL-ASSUMPTION-FORMS link for F1 and F2 resolves to not applicable.
Nested quantifiers. No family introduces quantifiers.
Sub-32-bit and oversize-literal arithmetic. No family changes numeric modeling.
